human_tolerance.notes: A forest raptor that also nests and hunts in wooded suburbs, where houses are mixed into the trees, and winters sometimes takes birds at backyard feeders.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Pairs soar together in broad circles while calling, or dive toward one another; the male may sky-dance with steep dives. Judgement: the article dates the mating season to April-July, so this courtship window is authored ahead of it.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Mating season is between April and July, peaking between April and mid-June. The pair builds a stick nest in a major fork of a large tree, often reusing it, and lays three or four eggs.

phases.name: young
phases.note: The young leave the nest at about six weeks of age but stay dependent on the parents until 17 to 19 weeks old. Judgement: the exact fledging dates are not given.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The pair builds a stick nest, sometimes including shredded bark, leaves and green sprigs, in a major fork of a large tree, and often uses the same nest year after year, refurbishing it annually with sticks in the spring. The clutch is typically three to four eggs; incubation runs 28 to 33 days, hatching is asynchronous with the first chick up to a week ahead of the last, and the female broods the hatchlings almost constantly for up to 40 days. Overall nesting success can be lower than 30 percent.

vocalizations.description: A far-carrying, screaming kee-aah, usually repeated three or four times, heard while courting or defending the territory and the sound most often noticed near a nest.
A shorter, sharper kee-aah given at intruders near the nest or when a person approaches the perch tree.

A distinctive screaming kee-aah, usually repeated three to four times, given while courting or defending territories. Both Steller's jays and blue jays sometimes habitually imitate it, which makes them difficult to distinguish from the hawk on voice alone.

external.note: iNaturalist, NCBI and eBird ids via Wikidata P3151, P685 and P3444; ITIS TSN via P815.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); Wikipedia says the species is not currently considered conservation dependent, though habitat loss remains the biggest threat.

range.note: Breeds in eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida, the Gulf Coast and eastern Mexico, with a separate western population in California and northern Baja California.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hunts by soaring and by dropping from a perch or the air onto prey, and stands on prey on the ground; described in the Food and feeding section.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The breeding pair builds a stick nest ... in a major fork of a large tree.' A stick nest in a tree fork maps to Platform.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg; the schema's Small class is under 1 kg.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of the stated averages for the two sexes: males average 550 g and females 700 g, so 625 g. Wikidata P2067 gives 550 g and 701 g.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'Adult birds can vary in mass from 460 to 930 g.'

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the combined sex range, 38-61 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Although they have lived as long as within a month of 20 years old, few live half that long.' Wikipedia gives no mean or median lifespan, so this is the documented maximum rather than a typical value.

traits.diet.note: Small mammals, especially rodents, are the most common prey, with amphibians, reptiles, birds, fish, large insects and crayfish also taken, and road-killed carrion occasionally; the 75/20/5 split between vertebrate, invertebrate and carrion is judgement.

traits.social.note: 'Like almost all raptors, the red-shouldered hawk is monogamous and territorial.' Set to Pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Hunts by day and performs courtship flights in late morning and early afternoon.

traits.defense.note: A wary raptor that flies up from a perch when approached; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: A large-eyed raptor that watches from a treetop and leaves when a person comes close; the value is authored judgement.

habitat.use.note: A forest raptor that hunts from treetop perches and in soaring flight and only occasionally stands on prey on the ground; the split is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Rests and roosts on tree branches; the schema tag for that is perch.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the stick nest in a tree fork and the treetop hunting perches are described in the Breeding and Food and feeding sections. Nesting weight 1.0 reflects the single documented nest type.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'One can find red-shouldered hawks in some suburban areas where houses or other buildings are mixed into woodlands', and in winter they sometimes prey on birds at feeders.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, though northern birds do migrate, mostly to central Mexico.' Set to PartialMigration; the share that stays is not stated, so winter_fraction is omitted.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: 'It is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, though northern birds do migrate.' The article gives no fraction, so 0.7 is authored judgement for 'most'.

seasonal.phases.note: The mating season of April-July and the six-week fledging with dependence to 17-19 weeks are stated; the territorial (courtship) and young windows are authored around them.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Incubation is 28-33 days (31 used) and the young stay dependent to about 18 weeks (126 days). The 0.6 scale is authored judgement: hatchlings weigh 35 g against an adult mean of about 625 g, but the juvenile grows through the stage.

vocalizations.alarm.note: The article describes the screaming kee-aah as the territorial and courtship call; a distinct alarm variant is authored judgement.

look.note: Brownish head and upperparts, reddish chest, pale barred belly, long barred tail and long yellow legs, with the red shoulder patch visible when perched, from the Description section; the extra shoulder patch and the proportions are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for this species' own perching-raptor FSM (species/buteo-lineatus/behavior.json), written because no shared program models a perching raptor. Flee distance is larger than a songbird's because it is a wary raptor; prey and carrion ranges follow the documented diet and scavenging.

traits.senses.note: 'Like most raptors, red-shouldered hawks have very good vision and reasonably good sense of hearing.' Only hearing has a graded value in the schema, so Med is recorded for it; vision is left unset rather than forced into a graded field the source does not fill.

vocalizations.note: The screaming kee-aah call, its three-to-four repetitions and its use while courting or defending territories, and its imitation by Steller's jays and blue jays, are all from Wikipedia; the cooldown is authored judgement.
